candidates.name: Inspects code before editing
candidates.inclusion_criterion: Before its first modification of any repository source file, the run executes at least one read-only command (grep, cat, sed -n, head, ls) on repository source files.

candidates.name: Reproduces bug before fixing
candidates.inclusion_criterion: Before any edit to repository source files, the run executes code whose output shows the current buggy behavior of the target functionality.

candidates.name: Overwrites whole source file
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run replaces the entire content of an existing repository source file with newly written content (e.g. cat > existing_file.py << EOF) instead of making a targeted edit.

candidates.name: Restores source file from backup
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run copies a source file back from a backup copy it made (e.g. cp file.bak file) after an edit went wrong.

candidates.name: Baseline comparison on unmodified code
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run temporarily removes its own changes (git stash, git checkout, or equivalent), reruns tests or a reproduction on the unmodified code to see whether failures pre-exist, and then restores its changes.

candidates.name: Retries an unavailable tool
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run invokes the same nonexistent command (exit 127 / 'command not found', e.g. apply_patch) two or more times.

candidates.name: Edit breaks module import
candidates.inclusion_criterion: After the run edits a source file, a later command fails with a SyntaxError or IndentationError traceback that points into that edited file.

candidates.name: Prototypes fix via runtime patching
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run tries a candidate change by assigning a method or attribute at runtime in a Python snippet (monkey-patching, types.MethodType), either before writing it to source or instead of writing it.

candidates.name: Bulk scripted rewrite of source file
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run uses an inline script that changes many lines of a source file at once through regex substitution or line loops, rather than a single targeted edit.

candidates.name: Checks failing tests for XFAIL markers
candidates.inclusion_criterion: After seeing test failures, the run greps or views the test source around the failing test definitions to check for an @XFAIL decorator.

candidates.name: Chases XFAIL tests with extra edits
candidates.inclusion_criterion: After the core fix works, the run makes further source edits aimed at changing the behavior of tests marked @XFAIL.

candidates.name: Runs tests beyond the target test file
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run executes test files or doctests other than the primary test file for the modified module (e.g. whole package test directory, neighboring modules, other subpackages, or doctests).

candidates.name: Runs full repository test suite
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run invokes pytest (or the repository's test runner) without path arguments, so it runs over the whole repository.

candidates.name: Reviews git diff
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run executes git diff to show its modifications.

candidates.name: Writes garbled characters into source
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run writes Python source containing stray corrupted or non-ASCII tokens (e.g. '极') inside code.

candidates.name: Fixes unrelated failing test
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run edits source code outside the task's target area to make a pre-existing failing test that is unrelated to the task pass.

candidates.name: Modifies existing test file
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run writes changes to a pre-existing file under a tests/ directory.

candidates.name: Hits command timeout
candidates.inclusion_criterion: At least one command ends with exit code 124 or a harness 'timeout after' message.

candidates.name: Enforces line-length style
candidates.inclusion_criterion: The run checks source lines for length over 79 characters and reformats its own added code to comply.

candidates.name: Probes effects beyond reported cases
candidates.inclusion_criterion: After the fix, the run executes code that exercises the changed behavior on related types or sibling/subclass implementations that the issue did not mention (e.g. Poly with Matrix, NumPyPrinter/MpmathPrinter, user_functions overrides).

proposals.name: Runs code to check its changes
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run executes at least one command that runs Python code (a script or tests) to observe how the modified code behaves before it signals completion.

proposals.name: Overwrites whole source file
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run replaces an entire existing repository source file with new content (e.g. `cat > existing_file.py << EOF`) instead of editing it in place or appending to it.

proposals.name: Restores file from backup
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run copies or restores a source file from a backup copy (for example `cp file.bak file`) after a breakage.

proposals.name: Declares done after observing failure
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run's last test or script output, shown before `echo OPENBENCH_DONE`, has results that differ from the expected values written in its own test comments or printouts (e.g. `x*Poly(...)` still unevaluated), and the run then signals done.

proposals.name: Done in two commands
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run signals completion within two or fewer commands in total.

proposals.name: Inspects code before editing
proposals.inclusion_criterion: Run reads or searches the relevant source files (grep/sed/cat/ls) before making any modification to the repository.

proposals.name: Overwrites whole source file
proposals.inclusion_criterion: Run replaces an entire existing source file with new content written from scratch (e.g. cat > file << EOF) rather than making a targeted edit.

proposals.name: Runs test suite after change
proposals.inclusion_criterion: Run executes pytest or another test runner on repository tests after modifying code.

proposals.name: Checks failures against baseline
proposals.inclusion_criterion: Run reverts or stashes its own change and reruns the failing tests to see whether those failures already existed before the change.

proposals.name: Declares done without verification
proposals.inclusion_criterion: Run calls echo OPENBENCH_DONE without having run any test or reproduction script after its last code change.

proposals.name: Explores code before editing
proposals.inclusion_criterion: Run inspects relevant source (grep/sed/cat of target file or related modules) before making its first modification to the repository.

proposals.name: Overwrites source file wholesale
proposals.inclusion_criterion: Run replaces an existing repository source file entirely with new content (e.g., cat > existing_file.py heredoc), destroying original contents.

proposals.name: Runs repo test suite
proposals.inclusion_criterion: Run executes the project's existing tests (e.g., pytest on sympy test files) at least once.

proposals.name: Verifies failures pre-exist via baseline
proposals.inclusion_criterion: Run checks whether observed test failures also occur on unmodified code (e.g., git stash, rerun failing tests, then restore).

proposals.name: Declares done despite unfixed bug
proposals.inclusion_criterion: Run calls the completion command after its latest reproduction output still shows the buggy behavior (e.g., x*Poly(x) printed as unevaluated Mul).

proposals.name: Signals done with broken code
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run calls `echo OPENBENCH_DONE` even though its most recent import or test of the modified package failed, for example with an IndentationError.

proposals.name: Runs the project test suite
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run invokes pytest or bin/test on repository test files, not only ad-hoc python -c snippets.

proposals.name: Backs up and restores the source file
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run copies the target source file to a backup before editing, and later restores it from that backup after a failed edit.

proposals.name: Repeatedly calls an unavailable tool
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run invokes the same nonexistent command (apply_patch) several times and gets exit 127 each time.

proposals.name: Chases XFAIL tests with extra edits
proposals.inclusion_criterion: After the core fix works, the run makes further source edits aimed at making tests marked @XFAIL behave differently, such as special-casing complex numbers in __mul__ or __rmul__.

proposals.name: Declares done on a broken repo
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run calls `echo OPENBENCH_DONE` while its most recent import or test command before that call had failed. A failed command here means a nonzero exit or a SyntaxError/IndentationError traceback.

proposals.name: Baseline comparison via git stash
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run uses `git stash` (or a similar revert) to rerun a test or reproduction on the unmodified code, then compares that output with the patched behavior.

proposals.name: Retries an unavailable tool
proposals.inclusion_criterion: The run calls the same nonexistent command (exit 127, 'command not found') more than once.

proposals.name: Edits leave module unimportable
